title: Highway Pursuit
project: A cinematic street race and car chase through a wet New York night after the rain: four cars, the police, a tunnel, a flyover and an escape, written as a listening piece for an eight-channel 7.1 system
brief: A street race that the police see; four cars (a Mustang, a Ferrari, a Lamborghini and a Porsche) at different speeds up to 150 km/h, one of them at one speed all the way; streets, a tunnel, cuts, bumps and a flyover edge; evaded at the end. The road is wet after the rain, nothing is falling, no wipers. The camera changes: inside the car, at the kerb, beside the cars and from a helicopter. Music in front, effects and fx behind it; a film mix; ten channels.
audience: a listener on a 7.1 system or headphones who came for the chase
purpose: keep the viewer leaning forward for a minute and land on a cut to black
point_of_view: the Hero's, over the bars: the music is what the rider hears, not a narrator's comment
job: a 60 s title-sequence cue for a motorcycle chase on an Indian national highway: the Hero is already evading when the cue starts, the villain closes, and every twist, drift and slow-motion beat is played by the music - no sound effects
story: Four cars race on a wet avenue (Ferrari flat-plane V8, Lamborghini V10, Mustang cross-plane V8, Porsche flat-six); a cruiser at the kerb sees the speeding and the chase begins. The Mustang runs out of road at the tunnel mouth. A helicopter joins. On the flyover the Ferrari jumps the edge in slow motion and lands; the Lamborghini loses the road. The cruisers stop and the Ferrari is evaded.

motifs.name: the_cell
motifs.shape: root, minor 3rd, fourth falling to the third, fifth: two bars; fragmented at the twist, stretched in slow motion, inverted over the flyover
motifs.why: four notes survive engine noise, a cut and a tempo change

references: night_pursuit_cinematic: the same chase grammar, rewritten for a highway, a colder colour and a real slow-motion beat

spatial_staging.why: the bikes are in front of the viewer and the percussion is behind: that is what makes the seat feel uncomfortable rather than loud

immersive.why: the chase surrounds the listener: the bikes swap the lead across the front, the tunnel closes the field, the flyover opens it and lifts the percussion overhead

anchors.why: the road is fixed under the viewer
the Hero is in front of the camera for the whole cue

movers.path: hard left rear to hard right front over the twist

height_plan.why: height is used for the shot, not for decoration

room_changes.why: the camera drops to the tarmac: a close, dry field
bullet time: the room lengthens and the near field empties
the flyover: the tail opens and the percussion lifts
back to the open road, dry and close

sonic_picture.first_10s: already at speed: pedal D, 16th ostinato, a taiko behind the listener
sonic_picture.middle: the twist to Ab, the drift down a semitone at a time, then the full chase
sonic_picture.last_note: one low D, struck, left to ring

expression.performer: a session orchestra playing to picture, conductor taking the cuts from a click and the slow motion from the tempo map
producer_moves: ride the ostinato up 3 dB into the chase, not the whole mix
in bullet time, open the room and pull the 16ths out: the tempo drop does the rest
keep the sub under the trucks, not under the strings
expression.anti_generic: no riser-and-impact drop and no trailer braam: the twist is a tritone, the drift is a slide played by the strings, the slow motion is a tempo, and the silence is written

theme.name: the_cell
theme.shape: up a third, a fourth that falls to the third, leap a fifth, settle on the third
theme.variation_plan: fragmented at the twist, stretched 3x in slow motion, inverted over the flyover, two notes and a low D at the escape

gate_reason: a build-hit-release cue with a short motif, a pulse that never stops and one slow-motion jump: the cinematic profile, started strict, with a project profile of its own
notes: Sound effects and ambience were asked for in the brief: four cars, two sirens, a helicopter, expansion joints, a landing, a crash, the city and drips are presets from physical models. They are synthesised, not recordings; the research note says which numbers are sourced and which are starting values.

tempo.note: 140 BPM, at the top of the cited 120-140 chase band (Karanyi Sounds); the slow-motion beat drops the tempo map to 84 and back, so the bullet-time is played, not filtered

ending_note: cut to black on the low D, then a short tail: no fade of a fake climax
avoid_feel_note: no victory cadence, no comedy, no tourist colour: the cue stays cold and forward
palette: percussion: bass drum, timpani, taiko, snare, crash
bass clarinet: chromatic approach and a long fall
choir: open fifth in slow motion
